Class ListItemFormat

java.lang.Object
java.text.Format
dev.visdb.seesaw.models.ListItemFormat
All Implemented Interfaces:
Serializable, Cloneable
public class ListItemFormat extends Format
Use this to produce a string representation of an ListItem. Configure the order in which the list item elements are formatted, each element type, and optionally Format, with addElemType(int, java.sql.JDBCType, java.text.Format). After this object is created, by default element 0 is formatted with toString(). Start with clear() to set up a different formatting specification.

Each JDBCType can have a default Format specified; use setFormat(java.sql.JDBCType, java.text.Format) to set a Format for a type. There are preset defaults for the date/time types 

These builtin defaults use SimpleDateFormat; the initial patterns are:
   JDBCType.DATE        "yyyy-MM-dd"              ISO_LOCAL_DATE
   JDBCType.TIME        "HH:mm:ss"                ISO_LOCAL_TIME
   JDBCType.TIMESTAMP   "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss"   ISO_LOCAL_DATE_TIME
When an elem is formatted, first a format assigned to the elem is checked, then the default format for the elem type is checked, if neither is available, then toString() is used to format the elem. the default time formats use .

Use Format.format(java.lang.Object), where the argument is an ListItem, to get the String representation. Note that if format's argument is not an ListItem, then an empty String is produced.

This is compatible with GlazedLists AutoCompleteSupport.

Since:
4.0.0
